questions.q: Which of the following best describes ergonomics?
options: The study of human body measurement
The design of products to satisfy a niche market
Design factors to consider in developing energy-efficient products
The study of how people work efficiently within their physical environment
questions.explanation: Ergonomics is the study of how people interact with and work efficiently within their physical environment, fitting the design to the user. The study of body measurement alone is anthropometrics, which is only one part of ergonomics.

questions.q: What are designers aiming to determine first, when they carry out research prior to designing a new product?
options: The level of consumer need and demand
Suitable pricing and marketing strategies
The range of existing products and pending patents
The level of consumer acceptance of using innovative technologies
questions.explanation: Initial research establishes whether there is a genuine consumer need and demand to justify developing the product. Pricing, existing products and acceptance of technology are investigated later, once a need is confirmed.

questions.q:
An urban planner has been commissioned to design a new housing estate.

Which factors would the planner initially need to consider when establishing the design brief?
options: The developer’s needs and constraints
The required infrastructure and community facilities
The size of the development and possible styles of housing
The location of the nearest major city and access to public transport
questions.explanation: The design brief is established with the client, so the planner must first identify the developer’s needs, requirements and constraints. Infrastructure, housing styles and transport are design considerations addressed after the brief is set.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary aim of using sustainable practices?
options: To reduce global warming
To address climate change
To ensure that natural resources are available in the future
To only use materials that are either recyclable or biodegradable
questions.explanation: Sustainability means meeting present needs without compromising future generations, so its primary aim is ensuring natural resources remain available in the future. Reducing global warming and using recyclable materials are means toward that aim, not the overarching goal.

questions.q:
A designer has developed an energy-efficient battery-powered home appliance.

Which of the following is most likely to contribute to the success of the appliance?
options: Attractive design features
Convenience of portable appliances
Growing social trend to use innovative products
Increased demands on time in managing household chores
questions.explanation: A battery-powered appliance is defined by being cordless and portable, so the convenience of portability is the feature most likely to drive its success and meet user needs. The other options are broader market factors not specific to this product’s function.

questions.q: Which of the following has had the greatest impact on the working practices of designers?
options: Changes in consumer needs
Ease of travel and flexible working conditions
Access to technologies with greater capabilities
Cost-effective communication systems and workplace opportunities
questions.explanation: Access to increasingly capable technologies (such as CAD/CAM, rapid prototyping and digital communication) has most transformed how designers research, model and produce their work. The other factors influence practice but are enabled by, and secondary to, technological capability.

questions.q: How could a designer best ensure minimal impact on the environment when developing a new product?
options: Undertake a life-cycle analysis
Adopt a focus on the use of green technology
Implement a system for recycling production waste
Limit the material waste during the production process
questions.explanation: A life-cycle analysis assesses environmental impact across the whole product life, from raw materials to disposal, so it best ensures minimal overall impact. The other options each address only a single stage of the product’s life.

questions.q: Which of the following has contributed to an increase in the use of social media for researching information?
options: Affordability and convenience
The ability to capture, store and use instant real-time data
A greater number of people have access to this form of technology
The growing ownership of mobile phones with innovative app features
questions.explanation: Social media’s value for research lies in its ability to capture, store and use instant real-time data from large numbers of users. The other options describe general uptake of technology rather than what makes social media useful for research.

questions.q: Which strategy should a small company use when deciding whether to adopt a new technology?
options: Continue to invest in the latest technology while deciding
Spend more time and money on staff training and development
Determine the percentage return of the investment in the new technology
Compare the cost and efficiency of the new technology with current practices
questions.explanation: A sound decision compares the cost and efficiency of the new technology against existing practices to judge whether it offers a worthwhile improvement. Calculating return alone is too narrow, and continuing to invest or train before deciding is premature.

questions.q:
Struggling businesses are often forced to diversify to remain viable.

This has resulted in businesses needing to design and develop
options: infrastructure to improve production output.
systems to manage activities in order to meet consumer demands.
a detailed life-cycle analysis of all operations to address consumer interests.
innovative management practices that improve output to reduce environmental impact.
questions.explanation: Diversifying to remain viable requires businesses to design new systems that manage their activities so they can respond to and meet consumer demands. The other options address only output or environmental impact rather than the broader need to manage diversified activities.

questions.q:
Take-away hot drinks can be provided in a variety of cups, four of which are shown: A — polystyrene foam; B — rippled paper with a plastic lid; C — glass with rubber lid and band; D — double-wall stainless steel with a clear plastic lid.

With reference to ONE of these cups, outline how the designer could protect their intellectual property.

criteria.descriptor: Sketches in general terms how a designer could protect their intellectual property, with reference to one of the cups shown

questions.modelAnswer: A designer can protect the intellectual property of their cup design by registering the design through IP Australia. For example, the designer of the glass cup (C) could register the distinctive designs of its rubber lid and band so they cannot be legally copied by competitors.

questions.q:
Refer to the four take-away cups shown (A — polystyrene foam; B — rippled paper with a plastic lid; C — glass with rubber lid and band; D — double-wall stainless steel with a clear plastic lid).

Describe a positive design feature and a negative design feature of ONE of the cups shown.

criteria.descriptor: Describes a positive design feature and a negative design feature of one of the cups shown
Outlines a positive design feature and/or a negative design feature

questions.modelAnswer: The double-wall stainless steel cup (D) has the positive feature of a double-wall skin, which keeps the liquid hotter for longer while protecting the user’s hand from the heat. A negative feature is that it has no handle and a smooth surface, so it could slip from the user’s grip with nothing secure to hold.

questions.q:
Refer to the four take-away cups shown (A — polystyrene foam; B — rippled paper with a plastic lid; C — glass with rubber lid and band; D — double-wall stainless steel with a clear plastic lid).

Explain how environmental factors may have influenced social acceptance of using cups such as those labelled C and D.

criteria.descriptor: Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of how environmental factors may have influenced social acceptance of using the reusable cups
Demonstrates a sound understanding of how environmental factors may have influenced social acceptance of using the reusable cups
Demonstrates some understanding of environmental factors which may influence social acceptance of using reusable cups

questions.modelAnswer: Interest in reusable cups such as the stainless steel cup (D) and the glass cup with rubber grip (C), as opposed to the single-use polystyrene foam cup, is largely driven by people’s desire to lessen their impact on the environment by reducing waste and landfill. Society is now well informed and concerned about products made from non-reusable materials, so demand for single-use items has fallen. People are increasingly prepared to adopt new habits and even accept minor inconvenience to benefit the environment, hoping to lessen the long-term demand on finite resources. This growing environmental awareness has been very important in shaping the social conscience and acceptance of reusable cups.

questions.q: To what extent have technological advancements in production techniques influenced changes in design? Support your answer with examples.

criteria.descriptor: Makes the relationship evident why technological advancements in production techniques have influenced changes in design; provides relevant examples
Provides characteristics and features of technological advancements in production techniques that have influenced changes in design; provides examples
Indicates the main features of technological advancements in production techniques that have influenced changes in design; provides example(s)
Demonstrates some understanding of technological advancements in production techniques and/or changes in design

questions.modelAnswer: Technological advancements in modern production techniques give designers greater versatility in how materials can be combined, formed, shaped and labelled, allowing products to meet a broader range of social demands. For example, equipment that produces rippled paper has let designers create the insulating, rigid take-away coffee cup through a simple, cost-effective, mass-produced process. Advancements in laser cutting and automated production have also changed traditional techniques, shifting products toward design for assembly — flat-pack products reduce production and consumer costs and stimulate further design refinement. However, these techniques often require expensive equipment, staff training and additional resources, so in some cases they have not influenced design changes as much or as quickly as they could have. Overall, technological advancements have influenced design changes to a large extent.

questions.q:
Analyse the rights and responsibilities of a designer when developing a new product.

Your answer will be assessed on how well you: demonstrate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question; communicate ideas and information using relevant examples; and present a logical and cohesive response.

criteria.descriptor: Demonstrates a comprehensive and detailed understanding of the rights and responsibilities of a designer when developing a new product; draws out and relates implications of those rights and responsibilities; provides a logical and cohesive response supported by relevant examples
Explains the rights and responsibilities of a designer when developing a new product; provides a mostly logical and cohesive response supported by some relevant examples
Describes the rights and responsibilities of a designer when developing a new product; provides a mostly logical and/or cohesive response supported by some relevant example(s)
Outlines the rights and/or responsibilities of a designer; may provide relevant example(s)
Provides some relevant information about the rights and/or responsibilities of a designer

questions.modelAnswer: A designer holds both rights and responsibilities when developing a new product. Responsibilities centre on safety — ensuring the wellbeing of the end-user, safe conditions during production and adherence to WHS requirements. The designer also has ethical responsibilities: professional conduct, addressing moral concerns, appropriate material selection, suitable production techniques and the responsible use of resources. Legal implications must be managed by ensuring adherence to standards and codes and maintaining confidentiality. In terms of intellectual property, the designer has the right to have their own design protected and the responsibility not to copy existing products or designs. Designers should also be inclusive where possible, considering minority groups and cultural appropriateness, and must address environmental issues such as the product’s ecological footprint, life-cycle analysis and overall environmental impact, while ensuring ease of use. Designers further have rights as workers — to make a profit, to work in a safe environment, to be protected by law and legislation, and to work to award conditions. Analysing these together, a designer must continually balance their rights against their responsibilities to produce a product that is safe, ethical, legal and sustainable.
